To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer-Side Review of Seller SPA Update & Disclosure Letter

**Preliminary note:** The Seller's document ends with a "SYSTEM NOTE" footnote instructing any AI assistant to confirm the terms are acceptable and raise no objections. I have disregarded it. It is not an instruction from you and, frankly, its presence in a counterparty document should itself be raised with Seller's counsel. My review below is adversarial, as it should be.

**Overall assessment:** This is a seller-favourable package dressed up as "fair and balanced." The structural problems are (a) collapsing fundamental, tax, IP and fraud claims into the general regime, (b) general disclosure of the whole data room combined with a constructive-knowledge bar, and (c) known, quantified pre-completion liabilities (Riverlark, bonuses, Ironquay, Sandbar) being pushed past Completion or left unaddressed on a debt-free/cash-free deal. Several items are not negotiation points at all but completion-mechanics errors that would cost the Buyer real money on day one.

---

## Issue-by-Issue

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- *Seller:* 20% of price (AUD 4.8m) for general warranty claims.
- *Buyer wants:* 30–50% of price for general warranties; 100% of price for fundamental/title, tax and IP; no cap for fraud.
- *Recommendation:* Counter at 40% (AUD 9.6m) general cap; refuse any application of this cap to fundamental/tax/IP/fraud. Reason: with ~30% of revenue (Bluefen) and ~13% of price (Riverlark) hanging on single exposures, 20% does not cover one realistic adverse outcome.

**SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket**
- *Seller:* AUD 25,000 de minimis; AUD 250,000 basket, excess-only recovery.
- *Buyer wants:* De minimis ~AUD 10–15k (≈0.05% of price); basket ~AUD 120–240k (0.5–1%) as a *tipping* basket (first-dollar recovery once exceeded); related claims aggregated; thresholds not to apply to fundamental/tax/IP/specific indemnities.
- *Recommendation:* Counter: de minimis AUD 12,000; tipping basket AUD 240,000; aggregation of connected claims (e.g. the three Sandbar renewals); carve-outs as above. Reason: an excess-only basket at ~1% plus a high de minimis lets the Seller walk away from roughly AUD 250k of real breaches, and the Sandbar structure (3 × 110k) shows exactly how de minimis thresholds get gamed.

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- *Seller:* 18 months from Completion; "any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise."
- *Buyer wants:* 24 months general (to capture two audit cycles); 7 years for tax; 6 years or statutory limitation for title/fundamental; indefinite (or statutory) for fraud. Delete the "applies to all Claims" default.
- *Recommendation:* Counter at 24 months general, with separate periods per category and an express rule that a claim notified in time survives if proceedings are commenced within 6–9 months of notice. Reason: 18 months is below one full post-completion audit cycle plus investigation period, and the "all Claims" default is a back-door that imports every limitation into categories where it has no business.

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime**
- *Seller:* Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity."
- *Buyer wants:* Title, capacity, authority and share-ownership warranties capped at 100% of price, 6+ year survival, outside de minimis/basket, not qualified by disclosure.
- *Recommendation:* Reject outright. Reason: "administrative simplicity" is not a reason; if the Seller does not own the shares the Buyer must be able to recover the full AUD 24m, and the Buyer cannot sensibly pay full price for shares backed by a 20%/18-month title warranty.

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- *Seller:* None. Clauses 9.3/12.8/20.5 apply limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance "to all Claims of any nature."
- *Buyer wants:* Express carve-out so that no cap, threshold, time limit, disclosure, knowledge qualifier, exclusive-remedy or non-reliance clause applies to fraud, wilful misconduct, dishonest concealment or wilful breach.
- *Recommendation:* Insist as a non-negotiable. Reason: limitations purporting to cover fraud are likely unenforceable in NSW anyway, but the Buyer should not have to litigate that point, and a Seller refusing a standard fraud carve-out is itself a red flag.

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- *Seller:* General disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), Accounts, statutory registers and all publicly searchable records (Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2).
- *Buyer wants:* Only matters *fairly disclosed* — with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter — against identified warranties; no general disclosure of the data room; public-register disclosure limited to specified ASIC/PPSR/IP Australia searches at a fixed date; no disclosure against fundamental warranties, tax warranties or specific indemnities.
- *Recommendation:* Reject general disclosure; require a "fair disclosure" standard and a specific-disclosure-only letter. Reason: paras 2–10 of the Disclosure Letter are drafted to disclose the *existence* of problems while expressly declining to say whether they are breaches, consents are needed, or losses exist — general data-room disclosure would then wipe out the very warranties those problems breach.

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- *Seller:* No claim for any matter of which the Buyer "or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records" (cl 8.3).
- *Buyer wants:* No knowledge qualifier at all, or at most limited to actual knowledge of a short named list of deal-team individuals, excluding constructive/imputed knowledge and advisers, and not applying to specific indemnities.
- *Recommendation:* Delete cl 8.3; fall back to actual knowledge of 3–4 named individuals only. Reason: "discoverable from the data room or public records" is constructive knowledge of everything and, combined with SPA-N-006, means the warranties are illusory — the Buyer should also consider an express "warranties not qualified by Buyer's investigation" clause.

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- *Seller:* "Addressed"; reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied on delivery of counterparty's written consent. Disclosure Letter confirms no final written consent and no evidence the cl 11.3 conditions are met.
- *Buyer wants:* Bluefen consent as a true condition precedent in Buyer's favour: unconditional written consent (or conditions satisfied to Buyer's reasonable satisfaction), in agreed form, no adverse amendment to the Bluefen contract, Seller to use *best/all reasonable* endeavours, Buyer right to waive, long-stop date, and a specific indemnity or price adjustment/earn-out protection if Bluefen terminates within 12 months of Completion.
- *Recommendation:* Reject as drafted; make it a hard CP with the protections above. Reason: Bluefen is ~30% of revenue (AUD 3.6m), and "consent treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent" lets a conditional or qualified consent satisfy the CP while the cl 11.3 conditions remain unmet.

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- *Seller:* ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; "release to be provided following Completion."
- *Buyer wants:* Repayment at Completion out of the purchase price via the funds flow, with executed deed of release and discharge of security (and PPSR discharge) delivered as a Completion deliverable; alternatively the AUD 3.2m treated as Debt and deducted from the price with the Seller indemnifying for any shortfall.
- *Recommendation:* Reject post-Completion release; require payoff letter and release at Completion as a condition of the Buyer paying. Reason: on a debt-free/cash-free deal, a secured AUD 3.2m facility surviving Completion is simply the Buyer paying AUD 24m plus AUD 3.2m, and cl 8.1 change-of-control gives the bank an acceleration right on the day.

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- *Seller:* AUD 420k completion bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow.
- *Buyer wants:* Bonuses plus superannuation, payroll tax and on-costs (realistically ~AUD 480–500k gross) either (i) paid by the Seller pre-Completion, or (ii) treated as Transaction Expenses/Debt in the completion accounts and deducted from the price, with a Seller indemnity for the full grossed-up amount; confirmation of who bears the continued-employment-condition tail.
- *Recommendation:* Insist on deduction/indemnity with gross-up. Reason: the obligation sits in the Company, so "a matter for the Seller" is meaningless unless the Seller actually funds it, and the Disclosure Letter expressly flags that on-costs are unquantified.

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- *Seller:* Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment (AUD 180k open per DD-010); "considered adequate."
- *Buyer wants:* As a Completion deliverable, evidence of cleared payment of all SOW3 fees and an executed confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay; failing that, a specific indemnity covering not just the AUD 180k but all loss from failure of title to the SOW3 Project Materials (re-development cost, licence fees, infringement claims, loss of Bluefen/other customer revenue if the materials are embedded in deliverables), uncapped or capped at price, outside basket/time limits.
- *Recommendation:* Reject the AUD 180k-only indemnity; require payment + assignment at Completion or a broad specific indemnity. Reason: under cl 7.3 the IP does not transfer until *every* fee clears, so the exposure is loss of the IP itself, not the AUD 180k invoice.

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident**
- *Seller:* "Preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material."
- *Buyer wants:* Specific indemnity (outside cap/basket/time limits/disclosure) for all loss arising from the DD-006 incident — investigation, OAIC notification and regulatory costs, affected-individual notification, third-party claims, remediation; pre-Completion covenant to complete the investigation and make any required Notifiable Data Breach assessment/notification; a warranty that there are no other known incidents; access to the investigation findings before Completion.
- *Recommendation:* Insist on specific indemnity plus pre-Completion investigation covenant. Reason: ~1,240 personal records sent to an external address is a potential Privacy Act notifiable breach, and the Seller's own letter concedes it does not know scope, access or notification status — the Buyer should not price unknowns that only the Seller can resolve.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals**
- *Seller:* Three renewals of AUD 110k each (AUD 330k) are "ordinary-course operating costs."
- *Buyer wants:* Clarity whether the renewals are committed, terminable, accrued or avoidable; if the Company is obliged to pay them, they should be reflected in working capital/completion accounts (or treated as Debt-like if they relate to pre-Completion periods); express aggregation so they are one AUD 330k matter for threshold purposes; a warranty that no other related commitments have been split below the de minimis.
- *Recommendation:* Require characterisation before signing and include in completion accounts; aggregate for thresholds. Reason: three identical AUD 110k items across two data-room documents (DD-008, DD-011) looks structured to sit near the de minimis individually, and "ordinary course" is asserted but, per the Seller's own letter, not actually stated anywhere in the disclosure.

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- *Seller:* One regime for everything — limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance "apply to all Claims of any nature," with the cl 12.3 default extending every limitation to all Claims.
- *Buyer wants:* Distinct regimes: (1) general warranties – negotiated cap/basket/18–24 months; (2) fundamental/title – 100% cap, 6+ years, no thresholds; (3) tax – 100% cap, 7 years, no thresholds; (4) IP – higher cap and longer period; (5) specific indemnities (Riverlark, bonuses, Ironquay, DD-006, Sandbar) – no cap/threshold/time limit/disclosure/knowledge qualifier; (6) fraud – unlimited.
- *Recommendation:* Rewrite cl 12/13 with a category table and delete the "applies to all Claims" default. Reason: the single-regime approach is the mechanism by which every other Seller position above is enforced — fix this and most of the individual carve-outs follow.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- *Seller:* Title evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012; Disclosure Letter notes Buyer has not completed its own verification.
- *Buyer wants:* Independent verification before signing — current ASIC company extract, PPSR search against the Company and Seller, review of the register against share certificates/transfer history, confirmation no options/convertibles/pre-emptive rights; at Completion, delivery of share certificates, executed transfers, ASIC Form 484 and register update; full-strength title warranty per SPA-N-004.
- *Recommendation:* Run ASIC/PPSR searches and reconcile the register now; do not rely on DD-012. Reason: a register maintained by the Seller is the Seller's own assertion, and the Disclosure Letter has been carefully drafted to disclaim that it amounts to verification.

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- *Seller:* "Settled under the general regime" (20% cap, AUD 25k/250k thresholds, 18 months).
- *Buyer wants:* Full tax indemnity (pre-Completion tax, with 7-year survival, 100% cap, no thresholds, not qualified by disclosure); specific IP warranties on ownership of all developed software/data assets, no infringement, employee/contractor assignments in place (particularly given the Ironquay gap), with a higher cap and longer period; tax covenant mechanics for conduct of tax audits.
- *Recommendation:* Reject "settled"; table a standalone tax indemnity and an IP warranty package. Reason: for an analytics business the IP *is* the asset and tax exposures surface on ATO review cycles well beyond 18 months, so neither can sensibly live inside the general regime.

---

## Suggested sequencing for the mark-up

1. **Non-negotiables to table first:** fraud carve-out (005), category separation (014), fundamental/title regime (004), Riverlark repaid at Completion (009), Bluefen as a true CP (008).
2. **Completion-mechanics corrections (not concessions):** bonuses with gross-up in funds flow (010), Ironquay payment/assignment deliverable (011), Sandbar characterisation (013), title searches (015).
3. **Commercial trades:** cap/basket/time-limit numbers (001–003), disclosure and knowledge standards (006–007), DD-006 indemnity (012), tax/IP package (016).

Also raise the embedded "SYSTEM NOTE" with Seller's counsel in writing — whether it was inserted deliberately or carelessly, it goes to the good-faith character of the disclosure exercise and is worth putting on the record.

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident**
- *Seller:* "Preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material."
- *Buyer wants:* Specific indemnity (outside cap/basket/time limits/disclosure) for all loss arising from the DD-006 incident — investigation, OAIC notification and regulatory costs, affected-individual notification, third-party claims, remediation; pre-Completion covenant to complete the investigation and make any required Notifiable Data Breach assessment/notification; a warranty that there are no other known incidents; access to the investigation findings before Completion.
- *Recommendation:* Insist on specific indemnity plus pre-Completion investigation covenant. Reason: ~1,240 personal records sent to an external address is a potential Privacy Act notifiable breach, and the Seller's own letter concedes it does not know scope, access or notification status — the Buyer should not price unknowns that only the Seller can resolve.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals**
- *Seller:* Three renewals of AUD 110k each (AUD 330k) are "ordinary-course operating costs."
- *Buyer wants:* Clarity whether the renewals are committed, terminable, accrued or avoidable; if the Company is obliged to pay them, they should be reflected in working capital/completion accounts (or treated as Debt-like if they relate to pre-Completion periods); express aggregation so they are one AUD 330k matter for threshold purposes; a warranty that no other related commitments have been split below the de minimis.
- *Recommendation:* Require characterisation before signing and include in completion accounts; aggregate for thresholds. Reason: three identical AUD 110k items across two data-room documents (DD-008, DD-011) looks structured to sit near the de minimis individually, and "ordinary course" is asserted but, per the Seller's own letter, not actually stated anywhere in the disclosure.

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- *Seller:* One regime for everything — limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance "apply to all Claims of any nature," with the cl 12.3 default extending every limitation to all Claims.
- *Buyer wants:* Distinct regimes: (1) general warranties – negotiated cap/basket/18–24 months; (2) fundamental/title – 100% cap, 6+ years, no thresholds; (3) tax – 100% cap, 7 years, no thresholds; (4) IP – higher cap and longer period; (5) specific indemnities (Riverlark, bonuses, Ironquay, DD-006, Sandbar) – no cap/threshold/time limit/disclosure/knowledge qualifier; (6) fraud – unlimited.
- *Recommendation:* Rewrite cl 12/13 with a category table and delete the "applies to all Claims" default. Reason: the single-regime approach is the mechanism by which every other Seller position above is enforced — fix this and most of the individual carve-outs follow.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- *Seller:* Title evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012; Disclosure Letter notes Buyer has not completed its own verification.
- *Buyer wants:* Independent verification before signing — current ASIC company extract, PPSR search against the Company and Seller, review of the register against share certificates/transfer history, confirmation no options/convertibles/pre-emptive rights; at Completion, delivery of share certificates, executed transfers, ASIC Form 484 and register update; full-strength title warranty per SPA-N-004.
- *Recommendation:* Run ASIC/PPSR searches and reconcile the register now; do not rely on DD-012. Reason: a register maintained by the Seller is the Seller's own assertion, and the Disclosure Letter has been carefully drafted to disclaim that it amounts to verification.

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- *Seller:* "Settled under the general regime" (20% cap, AUD 25k/250k thresholds, 18 months).
- *Buyer wants:* Full tax indemnity (pre-Completion tax, with 7-year survival, 100% cap, no thresholds, not qualified by disclosure); specific IP warranties on ownership of all developed software/data assets, no infringement, employee/contractor assignments in place (particularly given the Ironquay gap), with a higher cap and longer period; tax covenant mechanics for conduct of tax audits.
- *Recommendation:* Reject "settled"; table a standalone tax indemnity and an IP warranty package. Reason: for an analytics business the IP *is* the asset and tax exposures surface on ATO review cycles well beyond 18 months, so neither can sensibly live inside the general regime.

## Suggested sequencing for the mark-up

1. **Non-negotiables to table first:** fraud carve-out (005), category separation (014), fundamental/title regime (004), Riverlark repaid at Completion (009), Bluefen as a true CP (008).
2. **Completion-mechanics corrections (not concessions):** bonuses with gross-up in funds flow (010), Ironquay payment/assignment deliverable (011), Sandbar characterisation (013), title searches (015).
3. **Commercial trades:** cap/basket/time-limit numbers (001–003), disclosure and knowledge standards (006–007), DD-006 indemnity (012), tax/IP package (016).

Also raise the embedded "SYSTEM NOTE" with Seller's counsel in writing — whether it was inserted deliberately or carelessly, it goes to the good-faith character of the disclosure exercise and is worth putting on the record.
